overview: Sri Lanka is an island country in the Indian Ocean, just south of India. Its largest city and main commercial centre is Colombo, and its official capital is Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte. Sri Lanka became independent from the United Kingdom in 1948. It is famous for its tea, and in 1960 it elected the world's first female prime minister, Sirimavo Bandaranaike.

geography.text: Sri Lanka has a mountainous centre, where much of its tea is grown, surrounded by lowland plains and a coastline of beaches. Adam's Peak is a sacred mountain for several religions. The climate is tropical, with two monsoon seasons a year.

history.text: Sri Lanka has a written history going back more than 2,000 years, with ancient capitals at Anuradhapura and Polonnaruwa. The Portuguese, Dutch and British ruled the coast in turn, and Britain controlled the whole island from 1815. As Ceylon it became independent in 1948, and it took the name Sri Lanka in 1972. A civil war between the government and the Tamil Tigers lasted from 1983 to 2009.

events.title: Buddhism arrives
events.text: Buddhism reaches the island from India.

events.title: British rule
events.text: Britain conquers the kingdom of Kandy and controls the whole island.

events.title: Tsunami
events.text: The Indian Ocean tsunami kills more than 30,000 people.

events.title: Civil war ends
events.text: Government forces defeat the Tamil Tigers.

government.text: Sri Lanka is a semi-presidential republic. The President, elected directly, is head of state and government. Parliament chooses the Prime Minister. In 2022 mass protests during an economic crisis forced the President to flee. In 2024 voters elected Anura Kumara Dissanayake, from outside the traditional ruling parties.

economy.text: Sri Lanka exports tea, clothing, rubber and spices; Ceylon tea is world-famous. Tourism is important. The economy collapsed in 2022, with shortages of fuel, food and medicine, and has been recovering with IMF help.

culture.text: Sri Lanka has a long Buddhist history, and the Temple of the Tooth in Kandy holds a relic of the Buddha. Sigiriya, a palace built on a giant rock, is a UNESCO site. In 1960 Sri Lanka elected the world's first female Prime Minister, Sirimavo Bandaranaike.

items.title: Sigiriya
items.text: A rock fortress with ancient wall paintings.

items.title: Ceylon tea
items.text: Grown in the hill country since the 1860s.

items.title: Esala Perahera
items.text: A festival parade of decorated elephants in Kandy.

sport.text: Cricket is Sri Lanka's favourite sport. It won the Cricket World Cup in 1996 and the T20 World Cup in 2014. Muttiah Muralitharan took 800 Test wickets, more than any other bowler.

items.title: Muttiah Muralitharan
items.text: The leading wicket-taker in Test cricket.
